recipes.name: Dynamite Halibut
ingredients_raw: 2 pounds halibut, cut into bite size pieces

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Set an oven rack into the center of the oven.
Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and a layer of cooking spray.
Arrange halibut pieces on the prepared baking sheet so that all pieces are touching.
Mix the mayonnaise, lemon juice, chili garlic sauce, sugar, soy sauce, and sesame oil in a bowl; fold the mushrooms and onion into the mayonnaise mixture.
Spread the mushroom mixture over the halibut pieces.
Squeeze one lemon half over the mushroom mixture; sprinkle with Kosher salt.
Bake in the preheated oven until almost opaque, 15 to 20 minutes; remove the baking sheet from the oven.
Raise the oven rack with the baking sheet to the next-highest level switch the oven to broil.
Continue cooking the fish under the broiler until the top is browned, about 10 minutes.
Squeeze the remaining lemon half evenly over the fish.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.

raw_recipe.headline: Dynamite Halibut
raw_recipe.description: This sushi inspired dynamite halibut is coated with a lemon-mayonnaise sauce and flecked with mushrooms and onions.

review.reviewBody: I was curious about this recipe, wondering how it would turn out with uncooked veggies in mayo type sauce....it was amazing!! My husband, who doesn't care for fish much, LOVED it! Used lite mayo and while sauce was a bit thin, was perfect with sushi rice and snap peas. Follow the recipe...it's perfect.

I made this and both husband and I thought it was delicious! I cooked mushrooms and onions first and then added to mayo mixture. I also added fresh spinach under the fish and we couldn’t get enough! Definitely will make again.

I didn't have mushrooms so I used fresh asparagus. It was delish! I would bake maybe 10-12 min instead of 15 next time, then broil. The fish was slightly overdone but because of the sauce, it was still moist and yummy. Perhaps I cut the bite size pieces smaller than intended. Will definitely make again and will try with chicken breast too!

Recipe was really delicious but I almost burned it and set off the smoke alarm. You only broil it for 5 minutes not for 10 minutes if you are just making it for 2 people. Also make sure to draw all the water off the halibut by drying it out with paper towels.

yummy! the few modifications i made were this: i sauteed the onion and mushroom before adding it to the white sauce. i also cut the mayo in half and substituted low fat greek plain yogurt. it was delish, the family also agreed!

Used this recipe with a combination of halibut and cod for supper tonight. Quick and easy to prepare - tasted great. Substituted a fat free, non soy mayonnaise and used Splenda rather than sugar. The broiling took less than 5 minutes. Would not hesitate to serve to company and/or use with another white fish.

I didn’t have mushrooms, but feel that the recipe was still delicious. The sesame oil gives it an Asian flavor that is great. Next time, I will slice the fish into thinner slices prior to cooking as halibut tends to turn out somewhat dry when cooking. The sauce makes it perfect, so make sure to coat the fish well. Also, I think a bit of Siricha mixed in with the sauce or drizzled over the finished product would make a nice touch.

I have no idea why this got rave reviews. Followed it to a T. There is so little spice it tasted like a pile of mayonnaise, onions and mushrooms. Makes me shiver to think about the leftovers sitting in the fridge. If you are even thinking of trying this saute' your onions and mushrooms first and add more seasonings. Fish and crunchy onions pretty gross.

This was one of the best recipes I've ever tried! I needed up cooking it for about another 5-7 min because the piece of halibut was fairly think. Added red pepper slices and garlic shoots around the sides and took them out after broiling and before the additional 5-7 minutes added of baking time.

I did change a few things: I used vegenaise instead of mayonnaise, because I wanted to cut out dairy. I also used extra chili garlic sauce, and toasted the sesame seeds. Thrown on a bed of fresh arugula, it was one of the best meals I've had this month!

Wow wow wow!! KEY is use a high quality Mayo. It will take your recipe flavor to the next level. I used Kewpie Mayo. Recipe is outstanding & perfectly balanced with creaminess & spice. The mushrooms gives sauce a “heartiness” my hubby loved. My 16 year old twins raved about the meal. My son saved the recipe to “cook for his girlfriend when I get one” … his exact words :-). A keeper meal. I paired with 10 Minute Garlic Bok Choy.
Followed the directions it was good, but think the onions need to be cooked a bit before adding it to the mixture. Also cut 5 mins off of the first cook, then 3 mins off of the broil time.
I just made this with African pompano instead of the halibut seems like this would go well with any firm fish, It was excellent, mom says this is a guest for dinner kind of meal...
This recipe was delicious! Did not take long to make at all and tasted like you were in a sushi restaurant! Will definitely be making this again!
Delicious! I did not have sesame oil, so I substituted avocado oil. Will be making this one often!

All great. Didn’t have chili garlic sauce so used sriracha instead. Came out beautifully and didn’t move baking sheet to top rack to broil. Just left in place on center rack and broiled. Turn out beautifully.
This was quick and delicious...I would sub yogurt for half mayonnaise ....would be good with any whitefish...will make often! Yummy!
This is a solid recipe! I've made a lot of halibut over the years and this put a fresh spin on things. Wife and kids ate it up. Will be doing this again and try subbing with the wine.

LOVE. One of my all-time favorites. I would serve this once a week if my husband would let me :-) The only problem is I can never find halibut so I usually use swordfish. Any other suggestions for halibut substitutions?
Good recipe. Easy and relatively quick. Kids liked it. Substituted cod but otherwise followed exactly
